newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end flat despite rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end flat despite rate cut.

text.p: SPI futures 2374 +10 US 30yr cl 6.59 -0.07
*Stocks close just off, rate cut widely expected and already priced into market. Volume 306.64 million shares, value A$617.78 million, 1048 stocks traded, 334 steady, 369 up, 345 down.
Australian shares ended barely changed on Wednesday after a widely expected cut in interest rates failed to excite investors.

While the well-telegraphed cut in local rates was already priced into the market, the maintenance of the political status quo in the U.S. after its national elections also failed to spark any strong interest.

At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 1.00 point lower at 2,360.6. The December share price index futures contract was up 10 points at 2,374 and at a 13.4 point premium to the underlying index.
Some thought the Reserve Bank may have made a larger cut than that seen, but others suggested the 0.5 percentage point cut was appropriate and left the RBA with scope to cut again.
"I thought 0.5 was pretty well on the button and may leave the way open for another one not that far down the track," said head of equities at Intersuisse, Andrew Sekely.
Sekely noted that investors seemed comfortable with President Clinton's re-election, given that the Republicans looked set to retain control of the Senate.
"He romped home and the Republicans won the Senate and that is about the ideal result," Sekely said.
General activity was unexciting in line with the moderate turnover levels.
Petroleum Securities, which gained ground after a strong first quarter profit result, its first since listing on the NASDAQ market, attracted some attention.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 16 to 15, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures and options trade improved dramatically on Tuesday's lacklustre performance.
Total options traded 33,198 (17,558)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 7,085 (3,954).

In other local markets, Australian bonds and bill futures turned mixed on profit-taking after the Reserve Bank fulfilled market expectations with a 50 basis point cut in official interest rates to 6.5 percent, the second easing this year.
By 4.45 p.m. (0545 GMT), the 10 year T-bond was yielding 7.185 percent.
The Australian dollar rallied 1/3 cent Wednesday as weeks of worry over rates gave way to relief when the Reserve Bank only cut official interest rates by 0.5 point to 6.5 percent.
By 4.45 p.m. (0545 GMT), the local currency was quoted at US$0.7908/13.
